title: How the Autobahn Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the Autobahn, Germany's federal highway system: its origins (credited to Hitler but planned earlier, with the AVUS in Berlin and the Italian Autostrada as precursors), early construction, record-speed deaths of Bernd Rosemeyer and Rudolf Caracciola in 1938, wartime use and postwar disrepair, reunification-era rebuilding, its size, speed limits and minimum speed, German traffic rules (two-second rule, left-lane passing, tire speed ratings, low-emission zones), safety, and the Porsche road-testing myth. The episode opens with banter and closes with a Facebook Questions segment featuring a holographic John Hodgman promoting his book That Is All, with mention of his tour dates.

segments.title: Opening banter and Kraftwerk
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Aretha Franklin, Kraftwerk, and The Big Lebowski's band Autobahn, then introduce the episode topic.

segments.title: Porsche test-drive myth
segments.summary: Chuck describes his brother's Porsche with a signature sticker and the myth that Porsche test-drives every car on the Autobahn. They find no evidence of that, but Porsche and car makers do use the Autobahn for road tests, and a journalist drove a Lamborghini near Garmisch.

segments.title: Origins and Hitler myth
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Autobahn is the German federal motorway system and debunk the idea that Hitler invented it. They cite the AVUS in Berlin, the Italian Autostrada, and the German Chamber of Commerce's role in coining the term Autobahn, and note Nazi appropriation of the plan.

segments.title: 1938 land speed deaths and early construction
segments.summary: The first stretch, Frankfurt to Darmstadt, was used for Grand Prix racing tests. Bernd Rosemeyer died in 1938 after setting a speed record, and Rudolf Caracciola then set a higher speed before Rosemeyer died on a later attempt. The Nazis built out the network, reaching about 1,860 miles by 1941 though wartime use was limited and postwar neglect followed.

segments.title: Reunification and size of the network
segments.summary: The Autobahn took its modern form after East and West Germany reunited in the 1990s. The hosts discuss its length (about 8,000 miles, roughly 12,800 km, with conflicting figures) and its ranking among world road networks.

segments.title: Speed limits and tempo limits
segments.summary: About three quarters of the Autobahn has speed limits, called tempo limits, in congested or rough areas. About 2,000 miles have no limit, with a suggested 130 km/h (80 mph) and a minimum of about 60 km/h. Horses and mopeds are banned. Drivers can still be fined for unsafe speed in conditions.

segments.title: German driving rules
segments.summary: The hosts discuss German rules: the two-second following rule, fines for driving while eating or drinking, left-lane-only passing and fines for coercing faster drivers, tire speed ratings, and the emergency lane being for emergencies only, with running out of gas considered avoidable.

segments.title: Autobahn safety and engineering
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Autobahn safety, the fatality rate compared with the United States, and good road curve engineering. Chuck describes driving at Atlanta Motor Speedway. They note the Autobahn is among the safest roadways.

segments.title: Environmental speed limit debate
segments.summary: Some propose speed limits for environmental reasons rather than safety. Angela Merkel in 2007 opposed speed limits and urged automakers to build more efficient cars. Some cities have environmental zones requiring stickers.

segments.title: Route 66 and closing content
segments.summary: The hosts call the Autobahn a companion piece to Route 66 and reminisce about 1980s car posters. The segment ends with a Garfield joke.

segments.title: Facebook Questions with holographic John Hodgman
segments.summary: Hosts answer Facebook questions with John Hodgman as a hologram, covering favorite Muppets, Kermit, The Muppet Movie, board games, mustache, Asian carp, and his book That Is All, plus his book tour dates.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give listener contact information and promote the Stuff from the Future video podcast.
